attachments.origin_landmark: superior border of the rib below (inner surface), from sternum/costal cartilage to rib angle
attachments.insertion_landmark: inferior border of the rib above

actions: interchondral (parasternal) part elevates the sternal ribs (assists inspiration)

functional_compartments.name: Interosseous part
functional_compartments.function_note: Runs from the rib angles anteriorly to the costochondral junctions; fibers oriented opposite to the overlying external intercostals (inferolateral to superomedial). Its documented action is expiratory (depresses ribs), unlike the interchondral part of the same named muscle.
functional_compartments.source: De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

functional_compartments.name: Interchondral (parasternal) part
functional_compartments.function_note: Short segment between adjacent costal cartilages, anterior to the interosseous part; despite being part of the same named muscle it is documented to act as an inspiratory rib elevator -- a clear real example of one named muscle containing two regions with opposite mechanical actions.
functional_compartments.source: De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe in longitudinal (parasagittal) orientation over the target intercostal space, most reliably at the posterior axillary line where the rib is most superficial; probe tilted to follow the rib's curvature. This is the standard approach for an intercostal nerve block.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Internal intercostals form the middle of the three intercostal layers, deep to the external intercostals and superficial to the innermost intercostals; the intercostal neurovascular bundle (vein-artery-nerve, superior to inferior) runs in the plane directly deep to this muscle's inferior part, just below the rib's inferior margin, superficial to the innermost intercostal/subcostales layer.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Two adjacent hyperechoic rib shadows with the hypoechoic intercostal muscle layers spanning between them; the pleura is seen as a bright sliding line deep to the muscle layers, moving with respiration.
structures_at_risk: pleura and underlying lung (pneumothorax) -- the standard named hazard of any needle advanced into the intercostal space
intercostal vessels running with the nerve just deep to this muscle's inferior fibers
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for this muscle's own belly was found in the literature searched. What is well documented is the ultrasound-guided intercostal nerve block, whose target plane (the neurovascular bundle) runs directly deep to this muscle -- included here because it is the real clinical 'injection approach' relevant to this muscle's neurovascular plane, not a claim of an intramuscular BoNT target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Kannan A, Srinivasan S (2026) 'Image-Guided Interventions for Intercostal Neuralgia: What the Radiologist Needs to Know', J Med Imaging Radiat Oncol, doi:10.1111/1754-9485.70151 -- review of ultrasound- and CT-guided intercostal nerve block/ablation technique; Ajmal S et al (2024) J Bronchology Interv Pulmonol 31(2):183-187, doi:10.1097/LBR.0000000000000937 -- prospective clinical outcomes of intercostal nerve block at the rib angle
